verdicts.band: p1_b2 (ПОДАТОЦИ ЗА ПРИМЕРОКОТ table, row between 'Тип на пакување: Рефус | Количина: 38 г' and 'Увозник:')
verdicts.note: Both readers give the same value, and it is correct: 'Сериски број: SCR012601*', with the asterisk straight after the code and no space. They differ only in the notes they added, and every note checks out. Reader 1's context is right: 'Лаб. број: 3160/2026' (p1_b1), 'Со писмо: 139/2026' (p1_b1/b2) and 'Број: 3160/2026, Датум: 01.06.2026' in the header. None of these is a batch, lot or serial number. Reader 2 says no P lot number appears anywhere. I read all 16 bands (4 pages; page 4 is the aflatoxin row, the signatures and the stamp, then blank) and that is true: SCR012601* is the only batch identifier on the certificate. Reader 2 also says the asterisk is not a row mark. That holds as well. The footnote 'Со * се означени резултати од тестирање добиени со неакредитирани методи' (p3_b1, p3_b2, p4_b1) uses * only for test results from non-accredited methods. No result row in the pesticides, metals or mycotoxins tables has an asterisk, so the * after the serial is printed as part of the client-supplied identifier. The register also uses batch codes written with a star. P060342 is in the filename only, not on the certificate. The register's link SCR012601 -> P060342 (icoa_register_2026-09-10.csv, issuance_schedule_2026-09-10.csv) is register-sourced and was not read from this certificate. Sample: 'SCRAMBLER-сув цвет од медицински канабис'.
